crime.value: Contract murder: hired killer Costa strangles blackmailer Roy Baxter in his bed after poisoning the guard dog; then Costa himself is shot dead by Mama Rosetti. Central question: how to eliminate a blackmailer and then the only remaining witness without leaving evidence.
crime.quote: His hands fastened to the throat of the sleeping man.

victim.value: Roy Baxter, a lawyer/blackmailer extorting $25,000 from Rosetti for an old killing — killable because he would never stop; and Costa, the hitman, killable because he was the last witness and held leverage over the Rosettis.
victim.quote: “His name is Baxter. Roy Baxter.” ... “He wants money. I know him. He won’t stop.”

closed_world.value: A tiny circle of knowledge — only Rosetti, Mama Rosetti and the 'mutual friend' know of Costa — physically narrowed to the small fishing cruiser anchored off the Connecticut peninsula and Baxter's walled shore house.
closed_world.quote: “No. Just me, Mama and our friend.”

culprit_and_motive.value: Costa kills Baxter for a $5,000 fee on Rosetti's commission; Mama Rosetti kills Costa to erase the last person who could implicate them, since Costa had deliberately made them accessories.
culprit_and_motive.quote: “What must be done, must be done. There is no other way. Always must a person fight.”

resolution.value: No official justice: Mama Rosetti shoots Costa twice over the heart, drops him overboard to the tide and throws the pistol into the Sound — the 'cautious boy' out-cautioned.
resolution.quote: She shot him, twice, over the heart.

investigator.value: Lee Costa, professional killer as viewpoint character — a meticulous planner who casts himself as investigator of his target, and becomes the final victim.
investigator.quote: “I’m a very cautious boy, Mr. Rosetti. I’ll check it out. Let you know.”

suspect_architecture.value: Not a whodunit cast; an inverted hitman tale with three principals — Costa the professional killer (means/skill), Papa Rosetti the fearful client (motive: buried homicide, blackmail), and Mama Rosetti, the quiet knitting wife who is the story's concealed operator and ultimate killer. Ziggy the bodyguard and Baxter the blackmailer serve as foils.
suspect_architecture.quote: "No. Just me, Mama and our friend."

red_herring.value: Mama Rosetti's harmless-old-woman coding — endless knitting, maternal fussing about coats and colds, serving dinner — misdirects both Costa and reader from her being armed and lethal; the repeated 'Cover up good, don't catch cold' reads as warmth rather than menace.
red_herring.quote: "Wrap up good," she said. "Don't catch cold."

clue_fairness.value: Fairly planted: Mama states her own creed of caution and necessity aloud before the ending ('What must be done, must be done'; 'I too am careful. You must be very sure'), and her knitting sits in her lap in every scene — the same lap from which the automatic is drawn.
clue_fairness.quote: "Careful. Yes. I too am careful. You must be very sure."

social_world.value: New York Italian-American underworld of favors and debts: a former speakeasy turned character restaurant, a 'mutual friend' who repays an old obligation by lending a professional killer at 'the wholesale rate,' patriarchal restaurant family with muscle (Ziggy) subordinate to the boss — but real authority resting with Mama.
social_world.quote: "I did him a favor once. A big one. Now he pays me back. With you."

alibi.value: Costa engineers a mutual-complicity alibi structure: he travels only by the Rosettis' boat, appears in public as a scouting 'salesman' and as prospective buyer 'Zweller' from Ohio, and makes the Rosettis accessories so no party can testify against another.
alibi.quote: "That will make you both accessories before and after the fact. Makes for a nice silent relationship in the future."

reveal_mechanic.value: Demonstrated by action, not explanation: Costa's own boast that no one else knows he is there supplies Mama the exact condition for erasing the last witness, and she draws the automatic from beneath the knitting and shoots him twice over the heart, disposing of gun and body to the tide.
reveal_mechanic.quote: "Yes," she said, pulling an ugly little automatic out from under her knitting. "A very nice night."

investigator_wound.value: Costa's professionalized caution is itself the vulnerability: his self-image as 'a very cautious boy' who has covered every angle blinds him to the only person he never assessed as a threat — the little old woman he condescends to and eats dinner with.
investigator_wound.quote: "I'm always careful," he said. "I'm a very cautious boy."

victims_enemies.value: Roy Baxter, a lawyer of dubious means, blackmails Joe Rosetti over a killing Rosetti committed long ago, demanding $25,000 in two weeks — a relationship of pure extortion with no personal history, which is what makes Rosetti (and Mama) willing to have him killed. Costa, the second victim, is 'enemy' to the Rosettis only as the last living witness to their guilt.
victims_enemies.quote: "It was a long time ago. I killed a man. Baxter found out about it. He wants money."

suspect_wounds.value: Rosetti's visible terror and prior secret killing make him the obvious suspect; Costa exploits this by insisting the Rosettis be present at the scene, deliberately making them accessories before and after the fact so they can never inform. Their own guilt is the vulnerability the crime activates.
suspect_wounds.quote: "That will make you both accessories before and after the fact. Makes for a nice silent relationship in the future."

unreliable_frame.value: Mama Rosetti's placid, maternal surface — endless knitting, fussing about coats and colds — is a sustained deception; her repeated 'be careful' and 'cover up good' read as warmth until the automatic emerges from under the knitting. The reader trusts the domestic frame she projects.
unreliable_frame.quote: "Yes," she said, pulling an ugly little automatic out from under her knitting. "A very nice night."

setting_as_constraint.value: Baxter's midtown office is unusable (manned elevators, foot traffic, late-hour businesses), forcing the killing to the walled Connecticut waterfront house — reachable only by water. The Sound's outgoing tide, the servants who sleep in town, and the guard dog define the exact window and method; the same tide disposes of the dog and later Costa's body.
setting_as_constraint.quote: "It was awkwardly arranged for a killing, with its manned elevators, people coming and going and too many late-hour businesses."

evidence_type.value: Deliberate absence of evidence: gloves, no gun (bare hands), poisoned meat scraps retrieved and thrown into the sea, dog's body towed out on the tide, no vehicle driven to the scene. Costa's counter-forensic craft is the story's evidentiary centerpiece — and Mama's disposal of Costa and the pistol into the water mirrors it.
evidence_type.quote: "A tiny portion of the meat was still on the wooden floor of the dock. Carefully, he picked it up and threw it into the sea"

technical_detail.value: Skin-diving craft: wet-suit top, hood, flippers, mask and snorkel giving buoyancy to conserve strength on a long swim; drugged/poisoned meat in a sealed plastic bag tucked in the suit collar to silence the boxer; rubber gloves on the belt; strangulation with calloused hands rather than a gun; tidal calculation for body disposal.
technical_detail.quote: "He checked the collar of his wet suit to be sure that the small plastic bag he had tucked there was still in place"

moral_ambiguity.value: Mama Rosetti kills not from malice but from a peasant fatalism about survival — she applies the same protective instinct to murder that she applies to fussing over coats and cold, eliminating the one man who could ever testify against Papa. Costa himself is a 'professional' who does only what he's paid for, and Rosetti is a quiet restaurateur cornered by a blackmailer he cannot pay off.
moral_ambiguity.quote: "What must be done, must be done. There is no other way. Always must a person fight. All his life. I know this."
